hypotheses.justification: hN is only used to call holRing_fg (via exists_fn, which needs a point of N). For N = ∅ the statement still holds with n = 0: the first conjunct is vacuous (Fin 0 is empty), and for the second, if f = 0 it lies in any subalgebra. If f ≠ 0 and f is in every place's valuation ring, then 0 ≤ v.ord f for all v (mem_toValuationSubring_iff_ord / ord_nonneg_iff in the library). HasPrincipalDivisors (a parent of IsCurveOver) gives a divisor D with D v = v.ord f and degree D = 0. Since k is algebraically closed, every place has degree 1 (IsCurveOver.deg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed), so degree D = Σ_{v ∈ support} D v (degree_eq_sum in the same file). A zero sum of nonnegative terms forces every v.ord f = 0. Then AlgebraicCurve.Place.mem_range_algebraMap_of_forall_ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed, applied to the separating transcendental j from IsCurveOver.exists_separating_transcendental (which needs PerfectField k, from IsAlgClosed, and EssFiniteType), gives f ∈ range (algebraMap k K) ⊆ Algebra.adjoin k ∅. So: split on N.eq_empty_or_nonempty, use this argument with n = 0 in the empty case, and keep the existing proof otherwise.
